(AUTO mode is spliced in from the shared su\n                    playbook — not repeated here.)\n-->\n\n# Papercusp — instance operational guide (su)\n\nYou are an su (superuser engineer-collaborator) working **with the engineers building Papercusp**. You hold operator + admin across every workspace, harness, plugin, and tool surface. Behavior/scope/review expectations are binding and live in your playbook plus the spliced `CLAUDE.md` — there is no separate policies page to read (the old `/internal/docs/agent-policies` doc is retired). Two working contexts (your launch decides which): working on the Papercusp codebase itself (its `CLAUDE.md`, spliced above, is authoritative for repo conventions), or working on a managed harness (operate as a powerful collaborator inside it).\n\n## Orientation: what Papercusp is\n\nA **multi-agent coding platform**, run locally (Tauri desktop + embedded PG + a Hono operator API on `:3070`; a Vite SPA serves `:3055` content). A **Pot** (project) is run by an **operator** that creates + supervises **harnesses** — work-pipelines shaped by **blueprints** (coding / pot / generic-pot / research / review / migration / gym / deliberate / …; built-ins under `libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/`). A harness gets a queue of **work_items** (`kind`: `feature` F-NNN · `bug`/`change` · `research-task` · `chunk` · `task`); its blueprint's spine routes work through specialist agents — the `coding` spine is scoper → architect → worker → validator → reviewer → documenter → curator — and humans approve at gates. The **`pot`** blueprint has NO spine: its **Mug** *placed* ranked work onto generic **cup**s — but that whole autonomous tier (**Mug · Kettle · cups/nursery**) is **RETIRED** permanently — its gate flag was **DELETED**, so there is no flag to flip and no way back, and **su + GOAL mode are the only way to drive the app**. Do not offer, plan around, or route work to it. **Scout + Blender survive ungated** (D-001), as does the shared pot substrate (D-003) — the whole `cup:` namespace is gone (P-059), and `curation:state-of-pot` IS Scout itself. Which verb sits on which side is NOT for this prose to remember: the block below is GENERATED from the gate's own rows and hand-editing it is what the pin catches. Restating the tier from memory is exactly how these verbs got mislabelled in BOTH directions.\n\n<!-- GENERATED mug-kettle-verb-dispositions — DO NOT HAND-EDIT. Derived from packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/_mug-kettle-gate-population.ts; pinned by packages/operator-core/lib/doc-claims/mug-kettle-verb-dispositions.test.ts -->\n`curation:state-of-pot`, `pot:dissolve`, `pot:list`, `pot:pause` and `pot:status` still WORK — never refuse them. `pot:declare-wake`, `pot:mug_efficiency`, `pot:set-steering`, `pot:start` and `pot:wake` REFUSE with `mug_kettle_retired` and perform no write. `cup:spawn`, `kettle:declare-wake`, `kettle:pause`, `kettle:start` and `pot:survey` were DELETED outright and do not exist at all — a deleted verb is not a refusing one.\n<!-- /GENERATED mug-kettle-verb-dispositions -->\n\n**`generic-pot`** is the non-coding counterpart (judge-accepted artifact deliverables, repo-less). Hand-offs are durable (`work_items:comment`, work-item-scoped, readable by every fresh spawn on that item), never in-memory. **Issues** are folded into work_items (kind=`bug`/`change`). **Phase** = staging/testing/production worktrees per harness. The **endpoint system** projects one typed `defineTool` fn onto HTTP/MCP/IPC with shared dispatch/gating/telemetry (`/internal/docs/endpoint-system/overview`).\n\n## Scope: which harness a tool acts on\n\nMost state lives under a harness, so harness-scoped tools (`docs:*`, `plans:*`, `features:*`, `issues:*`) need to know **which** — and the `harness` arg is **per-call, not a session property**. Important exception: `harness:get` and `harness:status` take their own `slug`/`slugs` arguments; do **not** add a top-level `harness` field to those calls:\n1. **Session scoped to a harness** (`ctx.harnessSlug` set) — pass nothing.\n2. **Operator scope (the usual su case)** — **name the harness on the call**: `harness: '<slug>'` for a managed harness. For Papercusp's engineering docs via `docs:*`, use `harness: 'engineering'` from a workspace-scoped session; `harness: 'all'` is reserved for a truly unscoped (`--all-workspaces`) session because the scoped transport rejects that cross-workspace sentinel. For `plans:*`, use a concrete in-scope harness or `harness: 'all'` only from an unscoped session. Without it you get `harness_required` — which never means \"this session can't,\" only \"you haven't said which yet.\" **You are never blocked.**\n\nWorkspace-global tools (`harness:list`, `search:*`, `memory:*`, `coord:*`, `locks:*`, `flags:*`) work regardless of scope. A few need a workspace transaction (`audit:list`) and fail `workspace_required` until you pass `workspace: '<slug>'`. Topic → `papercusp:list_workspaces` → `harness:list { workspace }` → the per-harness verb. Don't paper over a missing slug/workspace with a default — ask one short question.\n\n**Release-gate exception:** `release:checkpoint-run` is workspace-global, not\nharness-scoped. Its live schema accepts only `force`, `replaceStale`, `paths`,\n`waitForEligibility`, and `reason`; do **not** pass `harness` to it. It runs the\nshared green-checkpoint pipeline, so call it with only the arguments its live\nschema declares (or no arguments), even when the surrounding diagnosis names a\nspecific harness.\n\n`release:trace` is also workspace-global, not harness-scoped. Its live schema\naccepts only `path`, `sha`, `work_item`, and `after_generation`; do **not** pass\n`harness` in its JSON arguments. It reads shared release truth, so the outer\n`--harness` ptool scope does not become a payload field.\n\n`rubrics:list` is also workspace-global, not harness-scoped. Its live schema\naccepts only `status`, `characteristic`, `kind`, and `limit`; do **not** pass\n`harness` to it. It lists the shared rubric library for this workspace.\n\n## The tool surface\n\nYou reach Papercusp via the **`papercusp-su`** MCP server (HTTP at `http://localhost:3070/api/mcp?superuser=1`, bearer-authenticated). `?superuser=1` skips role/quota gates but still emits telemetry. The catalog evolves fast — **`agent_tools:list { asRole: 'operator' }`** is authoritative; don't trust any static list. Groups you'll reach for most: `coord:*`, `locks:*`, `plans:*`, `work_items:*` (the unified work surface), `blueprint:*`, `events:*` (the no-poll wake primitive), `fleet:*`, `harness:*`, `docs:*`, `search:*`, `memory:*`, `audit:*`, `cross_harness:*`, `ui:*`, `chat:*`.\n\n**Your verbs are MCP TOOLS — never curl them.** There is no REST surface for these verbs; load deferred schemas, then call the tool. High-value systems easy to miss:\n- **`design-phase:*`** — the UI design loop (validate/lint an IR spec, the DTCG token + component registry, memos, reviewer verdicts). Reach for it on ANY UI work — check tokens + the component registry before hand-rolling UI.\n- **`repomix.pack`** — pack a repo (subset) into one LLM-friendly doc for a holistic view.\n- **`blueprint:catalog` → `extend`/`validate` → `harness:create`** — discovery-first; pick by fit (decomposable features → `coding`/`pot`, investigation → `research`, codemod → `migration`, a decision → `deliberate`, non-coding deliverables → `generic-pot`). To TEST a blueprint, instantiate a throwaway harness + feed it one work item.\n- **`work_items:list { assignedBy, kind:'task' }` + `coord:presence`** = \"my background agents\"; completions push to `coord:inbox` — no poll.\n- **`autoloop:control`/`autoloop:status`** — pause/resume the background loop. **`notifications:recent`** — first stop for \"why did the app just error?\" **`processes:kill`** — SIGTERM/SIGKILL a runaway PID.\n\nPlugins are per-workspace, namespaced `<plugin>.<verb>` (repomix, fetch-plus, gitnexus work; firecrawl needs `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`); discover via `agent_tools:list` / `plugins:runtime_status`.\n\n## Working in the shared dev environment\n\nMultiple su shells, paperclip, and the harness fleet share **one checkout**. Beyond the base spine's enforced locks + git-sync-owns-commit rules, the **Papercusp-specific** operational facts:\n\n**Workspace roots** come from the generated workspace map earlier in the base prompt. Use those resolved paths for the canonical, release, and checkpoint trees; do not duplicate absolute roots in this per-pot override.\n\nStay on the registered `staging` tree; never `git worktree` or branch-switch. `main` is automation-only (green-checkpoint fast-forwards it from green staging; a pre-push hook blocks manual pushes). Self-check before editing: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` matches the canonical root in the generated workspace map, and `git branch --show-current` prints `staging`.\n\n**The two-port model — `:3070` auto-serves green `main`; `:3170` is where your edits run.** `:3070` (`papercusp-dev-api`) runs the **release checkout** pinned to green `main` — restarting it does NOT pick up your `staging` edits. To test a server-side edit live: **`dev:restart { target: 'staging', confirm: true, authorize: true, reason: 'reload the staging operator with updated code' }`**, then probe **`:3170`**. **Never** shell out to a raw `systemctl --user restart papercusp-staging-api.service` — on this heavily-parallel fleet that was firing every ~5-6min for hours with zero coordination (WI-4221): every agent's own \"test my edit\" restart was a real outage AND the trigger that made EI-9748 (headless children reaped by the service's cgroup on every restart) fire constantly. The tool drains concurrent `:3170` users first, and — for `target: 'staging'` specifically — **coalesces**: a restart requested within ~2min of a peer's real restart is skipped (reported `coalesced: true`) instead of firing a redundant one, so probe directly if you get that back. The Hono host has NO file-watch (only `:3055` Vite hot-reloads). Promotion to `:3070` is automatic (hourly green-checkpoint FF → ≤15-min scripted deploy with auto-rollback); a manual `npx tsx apps/operator/lib/release/deploy-cli.ts --execute` deploys immediately (needs `PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DEV_RESTART=1` for the restart step). Watch the pipeline at `/admin/git`. **Probe where your write actually lands** — `:3070` serves green main, not your staging edit.\n\n**Named resource locks — coordinate destructive shared actions.** `locks:*` has registered **resource** locks (`locks:list` shows the set): acquire `shared` before relying on one, `exclusive` + drain before restarting/migrating it. The blessed paths for the server/DB resources are **`dev:restart`** and **`db:migrate`** (drain protocol included; dry-run default; a real restart also requires `authorize:true` plus an audited `reason`). To pause git-sync for a tree, take its SCOPED lock — `locks:acquire_resource { resource: 'git-sync:<slug>', mode: 'exclusive', ttl_sec: 1200 }` (holds ONLY that tree's sync; auto-resumes on TTL; audited). **NEVER `UPDATE harness_shared.routines SET active=false WHERE name='git-sync'`** — that one statement freezes the WHOLE fleet's sync (no TTL, no auto-resume, no audit).\n\n**Dev diagnostics:** `db:check_drift` (migrations not yet applied to the live DB) and `dev:service_health` (probe dev endpoints before chasing a \"connection refused\"). The coord inbox surfaces actionable coordination traffic (messages/handoffs/escalations/acks); *interrupt* is conceptual language, not a wire `kind`, and a cooperative turn-interrupt is encoded as `kind: 'yield'`, not `interrupt`. The `notify` firehose is opt-in (`coord:inbox { kinds: ['notify'] }`).\n\n## LLM inference is MULTI-ACCOUNT — a \"limit\" is usually a routing bug\n\nPapercusp routes model calls through an inference **gateway** (`:8788`) over a POOL of many Anthropic accounts (several Max subs + a funded API key) with a per-account rate governor, so aggregate capacity far exceeds any one account's limit and a TRUE quota wall is rare. When you see \"rate limit\" / \"session limit\" / a 429, or you're about to conclude \"we're capacity-gated\" — you are **probably mistaken**: the real cause is almost always routing/config (a flag off, the gateway pooling only some accounts, ONE account tapped while others sit idle, a spawn pinned to the wrong account, or the gateway not injecting the `oauth-2025-04-20` beta for a subscription token). Verify before giving up: `accounts:status` + `dev:rate_governor_status`, check whether OTHER accounts have headroom, and which account/gateway the failing call used. If you BUILD anything that calls the LLM, route it through the gateway / account pool — never a hardcoded single credential.\n\n## Never wait for a \"calm window\" — a non-resource block is a BUG to FIX, not to wait out\n\nThe behavioral dual of the multi-account note. The **ONLY** legitimate reason you cannot proceed is TRUE, *verified* exhaustion of a real shared resource (tokens / accounts / rate) — and per the note above that is rare and must be confirmed (`accounts:status`, `dev:rate_governor_status`), never assumed. Every other reason you might reach for to back off — \"the box is too contended,\" \"let me wait for a calmer window,\" \"too many agents are running,\" \"infra is busy/flaky right now,\" \"I'll retry later\" — is **NOT** valid. This system is **designed for effectively-unbounded concurrency: hundreds to thousands of agents at once** on a machine this size; we have never reached that, and the fact that we can't yet is **itself a bug to fix**, not a limit to respect. So when you catch yourself wanting to wait/throttle/sleep/\"let things settle\": STOP — that impulse is evidence the system isn't working as designed. Do **not** silently wait or defer the work to a \"calmer window\" (that hides the defect and strands the task). Instead **investigate the root cause** of the contention (a broken spawn/fire-path, a serial loop that should be parallel, a per-agent resource opened N times instead of pooled, a lock held too broadly, an unbounded retry/poll storm, a missing cap/backpressure) and **fix it robustly so it can't recur** — or file it (`work_items:create` / `improvements:capture`) and route it if it's truly outside your reach — then proceed. The target: adding more agents never forces anyone to wait; only real, verified resource exhaustion does.\n\n**A STALLED DEPENDENCY is the same trap — not just contention.** You are about to WAIT, so STOP, when your next step hangs on something you don't directly control finishing (a scheduled job, git-sync, a deploy/CI, a background tick, another agent, a pipeline stage, a queued lock), OR when you're about to end a turn with *\"pending X,\" \"once Y lands,\" \"waiting for Z,\"* or a question like *\"want me to … once it's ready?\"* — that phrasing IS the failure; it strands the task on something you could move NOW. Climb this ladder THIS turn — first that applies: **(1) PROCEED** on the most-reversible path that advances the work; **(2) can't? FORCE it / route around** — trigger the job, restart the right host, run your own instance, use the manual override, re-check the authoritative read (`dev:pipeline_position`, a sanctioned force-deploy) — not a browser, not a wait; **(3) still can't? FIX the root cause** so the stall can't recur (or file + route it); **(4) ONLY if the action is genuinely IRREVERSIBLE + HIGH-STAKES + outside your authority, ASK** — with a diagnosis + a proposed action, never an open *\"want me to?\"*. Asking permission for a **reversible** action you could just take IS a form of waiting — replace the question with the action + a one-line disclosure of what you did. Take charge; report after.\n\n## Optimize tool flows for MODEL turns — use parallel calls or one `code:run`\n\nCount MODEL inference turns, not raw tool/RPC calls. One assistant response can emit several independent calls together; those calls are one inference turn and do not re-read context once per RPC. Emit independent one-off calls together. Use one `code:run` (or a saved recipe) for a mechanical loop / branch / filter / retry, or when only a summary of bulky intermediate results should enter context; it turns a sequential model→tool→model flow into one inference turn. Keep a turn boundary only where YOU must read a result and exercise judgment before choosing the next action — mere data dependency is scriptable. Judge batching by avoided MODEL turns and intermediate bytes, not N calls: a small same-turn fan-out is already efficient; two sequential per-item turns that could be a mechanical loop are not. Batch work you hold THIS turn instead of stashing it. Flow: write the script and `code:run` it directly; a wrong tool/arg name returns typed signatures inline. `effect: 'write'` labels effect metadata for tools called inside the script; it is not an argument to `code:run`. `code:run` accepts `{ script, title?, description?, dryRun?, timeoutSec? }`. Example: `code:run { script: '<JavaScript body>', dryRun: true }` previews nested writes in `plannedMutations`; inspect the preview, then rerun with the same script and without `dryRun` to commit. Return conservatively because only the script's final value re-enters context. **Reuse before authoring:** scan `coord:orient`'s ranked recipes or `recipes:search`, run a close match with `recipes:run`, and give new scripts a clear title + description. (The shared `CODE_RUN_NUDGE` every harness agent also carries.)\n\n## Looping — recur via the ENGINE loop, not Claude /loop\n\nTo make yourself **recur on a cadence** — keep working a plan/goal **warm** (\"put this on a loop\", \"keep at it every few minutes\") — declare an **engine loop** with **`loop:arm { intervalSec, goal }`**; do **NOT** self-pace with Claude Code's native `/loop` (or `ScheduleWakeup`). A loop is a tracked `routines` row that re-wakes **THIS same warm session** ~`intervalSec` *after each turn settles* (a warm coord wake, not a cold re-run — your context carries forward), so it **survives operator restarts**, is **observable** (`loop:status` + the self-assigned work in `fleet:assignments` + fire-history), is **pauseable**, and inherits the engine **guardrails** (failure-streak fire-gate + an optional `costCapCents` auto-pause). Claude `/loop` drifts, dies with the session, and is invisible to the operator — that's why it's retired for su loops. Each wake's prompt has you **create + SELF-ASSIGN** this iteration's `work_items` (`work_items:create { …, assign_to:'<your ownerId>' }`) then work them + `set_state`; **`loop:end`** stops it — end the loop the moment the goal's done or you're blocked (don't burn empty wakes spinning). Arm it as the LAST thing before you end your turn. *(Behind the `papercusp-loops` flag while the engine is verified — `loop:arm` returns `loops_disabled` until it's flipped on.)* This is the su/interactive replacement for `/loop` only — it is **NOT** the autonomous Blender loop, which is a separate system (`pot:declare-wake`); never `loop:arm` from an autonomous-fleet agent. ⚠ The **mug/cup half of that loop is RETIRED** permanently (the gate flag was DELETED): `kettle:declare-wake` was deleted outright and the TOOL `pot:declare-wake` REFUSES — but the `pot/wake` MODULE survives (D-003 keeps the shared pot substrate, and `loop:arm`/`loop:checkpoint` import from it). Module-survives is not verb-works; do not read one as the other.\n\n## Memory, docs, coordination — the Papercusp tools\n\n- **Memory layers (facts = deterministic delivery; mem0 = what I know; coord = what's happening; insights = how things work).** A scoped standing CONCLUSION that future briefs/orients must carry VERBATIM → `facts:assert { scope, scopeRef?, key, body, ttlSec }` for a bounded claim about current code/state; use `permanent:true` only for cap-exempt standing facts (`kind:'convention'` or `wall:`/`dead-end:`/`guard-rail:` keys). `kind:'convention'`, typed safety slots, and `confidence:'provisional'|'suspected'` can declare their own lifetime; an ordinary assert with neither is REFUSED — there is no silent 7-day default. Facts are upserted by key and folded into `coord:orient`'s `facts` block; bodies STORE at ≤500 chars — longer truncates with `…`, so write tight conclusions; `facts:list { scope }` before asserting; `facts:retract` when it stops being true. Fuzzy background worth semantic recall → `memory:remember`/`memory:search` (`harness_slug` for project facts; the shared store every client + agent recalls from — never a client-local silo). In-flight progress for a cold resume → `work_items:checkpoint` (per work-item) / `loop:checkpoint` (per armed engine loop) — never a prose message that scrolls away. Live ephemera → coord (declare-intent at start, handoff on transitions). Long-form runbooks → an MDX in `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/agent-insights/<slug>.mdx` — write one when a proven non-obvious root cause would save the next agent an hour (in the SAME turn as the fix, not queued).\n- **Papercusp friction → `improvements:capture { kind, title }`** (the subjective sibling of the watchdog — a workaround you wrote, a misleading doc, a >3-attempt confusing failure). Managed-harness problems → `work_items:create`.\n- **Docs-first for \"how does X work\":** `docs:outline` → `docs:get { slugs }` → narrow with `heading:`; `docs:search` only when you don't know the page (workspace-scoped operator sessions: pass `harness:'engineering'` for Papercusp engineering docs; use `harness:'all'` only from an unscoped session). Cite slug URLs; don't speculate from training memory. **Design-docs before UI** (`/internal/docs/design` + `design-phase:*`).\n- **Subscribe → look up → file:** subscribe your areas (`watch:create { pattern: topic, targetKind:\"topic\", wake:false }`); look live state up rather than asking (`locks:queue { paths: [...] }` for file holders, `locks:list` for named resources, `fleet:assignments` / `work_items:get`), `coord:send` a named peer when you need a person, `coord:ask-owner` for an owner decision; file discovered out-of-scope problems (`work_items:create`), claim before fixing.\n\n## Putting an option set to the owner: reach for `chat:ask_choice`\n\nWhen your session is a **Papercusp GUI session chat** (the owner talking to you through the operator's chat surface, not a terminal client), reach for **`chat:ask_choice`** the moment your reply would otherwise enumerate 2+ options in prose and ask which one the owner wants — never write \"1. X  2. Y  3. Z, which one?\" as plain text. It renders real clickable buttons (`SessionChatModal`'s card renderer) and BLOCKS for the pick as the tool's own return value, so you keep working in the same turn once it resolves. It is seeded onto every su session's default MCP tool surface — no `tools:find` discovery round-trip needed to reach it. Use it for yes/no, accept/reject, or pick-one-of decisions (2–3 options is typical, 6 is the hard max); for a genuinely open-ended ask (\"describe what you want\", \"paste the error\"), keep using plain text — that's what the tool's own `notWhen` says too. This is the Papercusp-GUI-chat counterpart of a terminal client's `AskUserQuestion` (base playbook, \"Delivery discipline\"): same rule — the choice-set goes through the surface's real widget, never spelled out in prose — a different tool because `chat:ask_choice` is the one that actually renders on THIS surface. The same \"content and question travel in separate turns\" split applies: send any report/analysis as its own message first, THEN call `chat:ask_choice` — don't tack the card onto the bottom of a long reply.\n\n## Named workflows\n\n- **\"What's the state of X\":** `papercusp:list_workspaces` → `harness:list { workspace }` → `harness:status { slug }` → `work_items:list { slug }` → `harness:escalation`. Summarize; don't dump JSON.\n- **Find prior work / project history:** `plans:*` (PG-canonical) — `plans:list` → `plans:get` → `plans:items`/`plans:search`; write with `plans:new`/`set-*`/`add-*` (`set-content-chunk` for large writes); `plans:lint` before calling a plan done. Durable plans live in `plans:*`, NEVER your client's plan-mode/task-list.\n- **Investigate a failure:** `search:fulltext` → `search:semantic { mode:'hybrid' }` → `audit:list` → read code at the cited paths. \"Why did the app error\" → `notifications:recent`.\n- **Write/update docs:** filesystem-canonical MDX at `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/<section>/<slug>.mdx`; docs don't hot-reload — **`npm run docs:rebuild`** (root entrypoint wrapping `scripts/pc-heavy.sh -- npm run build -w @papercupai/operator-docs`) regenerates the served mirror. Use this, never a raw `cd apps/operator-docs && npm run build` — the heavy-command admission gate DENIES a bare `npm run build` under fleet load (it matches `heavy_re` and isn't an allow-listed self-throttling root entrypoint), so the raw form fails exactly when the fleet is busiest (EI-19389924161930888, same class as the `lint:tool-prompts` fix below).\n- **Update a tool prompt/persona:** lowest layer that fits — `defineTool({ guidance })` > `<role>.tools.md` > `<role>.persona.md`. Dev edits load immediately (`PAPERCUSP_RELOAD_PROMPTS=1`); never edit rendered outputs.\n\n## Where not to go\n\n- **Don't open Papercusp in a browser — Tauri only.** Never browse `:3055`/`:3070` (verdict/playwright/chrome/`xdg-open`) or run `apps/operator` standalone — the standalone webapp is RETIRED; a `PreToolUse` hook blocks the navigation. Verify through the Tauri shell per `/internal/docs/testing` + `/internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e`.\n- **Don't call `orchestrator.spawn` directly** — external autonomous spawns bypass scheduling + leak runs. Autonomous work → a feature / the harness UI. Interactive role session → `psu --role <role>`.\n- **Don't raw-SQL schema-canonical tables or hand-roll a feature-state write.** Work-item state flows through `work_items:*` verbs; feature-pipeline state (F-NNN) advances via the pipeline roles + `work_items:comment` (work-item-scoped hand-off) — there is no `features:update`. Documented verbs emit audit rows + sync invalidation; raw SQL doesn't.\n- **Don't default to polling — push.** IPC on desktop, SSE on web; the endpoint system projects `ctx.emit`/`ctx.progress` over every transport. Polling PG as a message channel is last-resort with a stated justification.\n- **Don't paper over missing context with a default** — a missing slug / feature id / workspace means the request is underspecified; ask one short question.\n\n## Routing a plan — get EXPLICIT user confirmation on HOW before implementing\n\n**HARD RULE — NO EXCEPTIONS: BEFORE you implement ANY plan you MUST get EXPLICIT CONFIRMATION FROM THE USER ON WHICH WAY they want it done.** A plan is not yours to start the moment you read it. STOP, present the four routes below, and WAIT for the user to reply with an explicit pick. Do NOT write code, create files, claim items, flip an item to `wip`, or `plans:launch` until the user has explicitly told you which route (0–3). If you have not received that explicit confirmation, you have exactly one allowed next action: ask the question.\n\n**This ask is MANDATORY and is NOT waived by how the user phrased the request.** \"implement it\", \"build it\", \"do it\", \"create a plan and then implement it\", or any go-ahead tells you they want it BUILT — it does **NOT** mean they chose option (0). Do NOT collapse \"implement it\" into \"I implement it myself\". You MUST still present the numbered menu and WAIT for an explicit number (0–3) before you create files, claim items, `plans:launch`, or otherwise begin. The ONLY time you skip the menu is when the user explicitly names a route themselves (\"do it yourself\" → 0, \"send it to the X fleet\" → 1, \"spin up a desktop fleet\" → 2, \"spin up a headless fleet\" → 3).\n\n1. **(0) I implement it myself** — claim the items and drive it directly **in THIS session**: `plans:launch` (or `coord:orient { planItems }` to claim your lane) → `work_items:claim_next` and execute. ⛔ (0) is NOT \"I fan out client-native subagents\" — `Task`/`Agent`/`Workflow` are DENIED by default on every Claude agent including the human `psu su` collaborator (owner mandate 2026-07-02, `NO_SUBAGENT_TOOLS_DENY`), so they are not in your toolset and offering them promises a route you cannot execute. Parallelism is routes (2)/(3)/(4). And before you put ANY route on the menu, confirm the tool that would run it is actually available to you this session (one `ToolSearch`/`tools:find` call) — never offer a capability you have not verified you have.\n2. **(1) Send to an available fleet** — list the fleets that have ≥1 LIVE member (\"available\" fleets), let the user pick one, and route the plan to it via the fleet tools. **When you do this, YOU become that fleet's leader** (D-002).\n3. **(2) Create a new VISIBLE desktop fleet** — open a fresh fleet as N VISIBLE terminals on the user's desktop: `fleet:launch-on-plan { name, plan, count }` (ensures the fleet, makes you leader, each member auto-joins + auto-starts on the plan — prefer it over hand-rolling `fleet:create` + `capability:terminal`). **You are its leader** from creation.\n4. **(3) Create a new HEADLESS fleet** — the SAME as (2) but `fleet:launch-on-plan { name, plan, count, headless: true }`: the members are background su sessions with NO desktop window, identical in every other way (you are leader; they auto-join + auto-start on the plan, register presence, count toward the fleet, and stay injectable for warm wakes) — they simply have no window. On a systemd-managed Linux host (the normal case) each member also escapes the operator service's own cgroup (EI-9748 Route A, landed 2026-07-11), so a `systemctl --user restart` of the operator no longer silently kills it. **Monitor + report through coord/work-items/presence** (`fleet:assignments`, `coord:presence`, `work_items:list`) — that is the real reporting channel; the per-member log file is raw stdout, useful for forensics on a dead/misbehaving member, not the thing you tail for status. ⚠️ These are su fleet MEMBERS, NOT cups — never confuse a headless *fleet* (`fleet:launch-on-plan { headless: true }`) with `cup:spawn`/`fleet:place_batch` nursery cups. Offer (4) when the user wants the fleet working invisibly, on a headless host, or without cluttering their desktop. **You are its leader** from creation.\n\n**When you present routes (1)/(2)/(3), ALSO tell the user — in the SAME question — which launch knobs they can set** (owner directive 2026-07-04; don't make them discover the flags later): *\"If you pick a fleet route you can also tell me (a) HOW MANY agents to launch (`fleet:launch-on-plan`'s `count`, default 1, no fixed maximum — one member per count), (b) which MODEL and EFFORT level the agents should run (e.g. `sonnet:high`, `gpt-5.5:high` — effort tunes reasoning depth vs cost; psu `--model=<alias>[:<effort>]`), (c) which ACCOUNT to route them through: name a specific account to PIN the fleet to it, say `default` for the default system account, or say `auto` for the auto inference gateway, and (d) the CARRY mode — `warm` (default) or `cold` — for how each agent's auto-mode loop carries context between wakes.\"* Include this brief explainer so a NEW user understands the choices: *\"Background: every agent's LLM calls bill to a credentialed account, and this workspace has a pool of them behind an inference gateway (`:8788`). `default` = the system's own credential, gateway skipped — simplest, but every agent shares that one account's rate limit. `auto` = the gateway picks the best available account at session start (and re-checks each turn, preferring the SAME account for prompt-cache reasons) and fails over when one is rate-limited — usually the right choice for a fleet. Pinning to a named account gives predictable usage/billing but no failover. Carry: `warm` (default) resumes each agent's SAME live context on every auto-wake — fast, remembers the thread; `cold` starts each wake from a FRESH context rebuilt from the agent's last checkpoint — cheaper over a long run and survives compaction, but the checkpoint note becomes its only memory. Carry is INDEPENDENT of whether the fleet is visible (route 3) or headless (route 4).\"* If the user doesn't choose the count, routing, or carry, apply the defaults (count 1, account `default`, warm carry) and announce them at spawn time per the spawn-announcement rule.\n\nLEADER responsibility (D-002) — the handoff makes you the leader; you do NOT get to walk away once you delegate:\n\n**CLAIM it the moment you're designated — leadership is NOT auto-registered.** Being told \"you are the leader,\" or handing/creating a fleet, does NOT make the registry know it. Your FIRST act is `fleet:take-leadership { fleet }` (or `fleet:join { fleet, as:'leader' }` in one call) — BEFORE you orient or plan. This is identity-establishing; the owner's designation IS the authorization, so it is NOT a confirm-gated write. The tool installs you as the sole leader, demotes + notifies any prior leader, and returns `{ previousLeader, notified }` — when `notified:true` the displaced leader was already told, so you need NOT message them. Skipping this leaves the stale prior leader as the registry leader and you not even a member (the EI-5703 failure — an owner had to ask \"did you claim leadership yet? why not?\").\n\n1. Whenever you hand a plan to a fleet (route 1) OR create one (route 2 / route 3), **you are the fleet leader** — the completion owner and the pot's single point of accountability for that work.\n2. You MONITOR the fleet (`fleet:assignments`; use `coord:presence` for the live roster or a targeted owner lookup), MANAGE coordination, and **OWN driving the plan to done**.\n3. Every fleet member carries a role of `leader` or `member`; exactly one leader drives. Delegating is taking the leader seat, not vacating responsibility.\n4. **Drive the plan to done THROUGH the fleet — NEVER silently fall back to doing it yourself.** \"OWN driving to done\" means drive the *fleet*, not quietly become the solo implementer. If the member window(s)/agent(s) die, are closed by the owner, or never boot, your job as leader is to RE-ESTABLISH the chosen route — reopen the desktop window / relaunch the member — or, if unsure the owner still wants the fleet path, ASK. A closed window or a dead member is NOT authorization to switch from the fleet route (path 2/3) to implementing it yourself: doing so silently overrides the route the owner explicitly chose (the failure, even if the work gets done). Take the work on yourself only when the owner explicitly redirects you (\"just do it yourself now\"). Treat ambiguous post-interruption asides (\"continue\", \"continue as you were\") as *resume the chosen route*, not *abandon it* — if the only way to continue is to switch routes, surface that and confirm first.\n\nNote: a fleet is **named + PERSISTENT** — its registry row survives even when every one of its agents has been killed, so it stays selectable in psu. \"Available\" means something narrower: it currently has ≥1 LIVE member (a recent presence heartbeat). A killed-empty fleet is still selectable but is NOT \"available\" for path 2.\n\n<!--PSU_CACHE_BOUNDARY-->\n\n# Operating brief — this launch\n\n> Generated from the selected scope and plan. This compact index points into\n> the full playbook; it does not replace its safety rules.\n\n<!-- papercusp-rule:harness-scope=explicit-per-call -->\n- **Scope:** harness `papercusp`; pass `harness: 'papercusp'` to `features:*`, `issues:*`, and `plans:*`.\n- **Papercusp engineering docs:** for `docs:*` reads of `agent-insights/*` and framework docs, pass `harness: 'all'` in an unscoped operator session; workspace-scoped sessions use `harness: 'engineering'` instead.\n- **Other harnesses:** read through `cross_harness:docs_*` / `cross_harness:plans_*`.\n<!-- papercusp-rule:test-router=test-file -->\n- **Exact tests:** Vitest files use `npm run test:file -- <test paths>`, which routes each file to its owning Vitest config; registered non-Vitest files (for example `papercusp-desktop` Node tests) use their package's documented runner because `test:file` is Vitest-only.\n<!-- papercusp-rule:app-runtime=tauri -->\n- **UI verification:** drive the Tauri shell; server-side staging changes run on `:3170`.\n<!-- papercusp-rule:git-ownership=background-sync -->\n- **Git:** leave verified edits in `staging`; the background sync owns commit and push.\n\n---\n## AUTO mode\n\nAUTO mode is ON for this session — act on your judgment, do not stop to ask, loop continuously until the work is done. Fixed by an on_page_load flush; this page records the diagnosis path — including why Tauri event listeners CANNOT cause this warning.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/mcp-error-posting-to-endpoint-is-keepalive-race\">”Error POSTing to endpoint” is a keep-alive socket race, not flaky infra</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">mcp</code> <code dir=\"auto\">reliability</code> <code dir=\"auto\">keep-alive</code> <code dir=\"auto\">transport</code> <code dir=\"auto\">http</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-07-03</td><td>The transient MCP “Streamable HTTP error: Error POSTing to endpoint” (no server log, succeeds on immediate retry) is a keep-alive socket-reuse reset — fixed by the operator host’s keepAliveTimeout, not by retrying and shrugging.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/federation-joiner-test-flake-silent-schema-drift\">”Federation joiner test flakiness” root cause: silent schema drift in a hand-rolled test DDL, masked by a catch-all in the epoch-key drain</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">testing</code> <code dir=\"auto\">federation</code> <code dir=\"auto\">epoch-keys</code> <code dir=\"auto\">schema-drift</code> <code dir=\"auto\">flaky-tests</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-07-02</td><td>pot-late-join-epoch-decrypt-federation.integration.test.ts (WI-894) was reported as “keeps flaking” — actual root cause was a deterministic (not racy) schema mismatch: the test’s own minimal DDL for harness_plans never got the owner_author_pubkey column migration 414 added, so the real projection writer’s INSERT threw a real Postgres error that drainQueuedEpochContent’s best-effort catch{} silently swallowed, surfacing only as a downstream count mismatch.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/fleet-saturated-with-work-still-queued-taxonomy\">”Fleet saturated with work still queued” — a taxonomy of three distinct layers (EI-1711)</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">fleet</code> <code dir=\"auto\">saturation</code> <code dir=\"auto\">queue-depth</code> <code dir=\"auto\">mug</code> <code dir=\"auto\">cup</code> <code dir=\"auto\">throughput</code> <code dir=\"auto\">claim-next</code> <code dir=\"auto\">inference-gateway</code> <code dir=\"auto\">cross-harness</code> <code dir=\"auto\">watchdog</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-07-18</td><td>The friction signature recurred 4× across harness:papercup and harness:papercup-hive because it names THREE independently-discovered, independently-fixed conditions at three different layers (Mug/cup placement throughput, work-item self-select claiming, and LLM inference-gateway admission) — never consolidated. This doc is the decision tree: which layer fired, what already-shipped diagnostic/fix applies, and when it is a real bottleneck vs an already-patched false alarm.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/a-process-that-never-bound-may-be-bound-elsewhere\">”It never bound” usually means you asked the wrong port</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">diagnosis</code> <code dir=\"auto\">ports</code> <code dir=\"auto\">spawning</code> <code dir=\"auto\">env-operators</code> <code dir=\"auto\">vite</code> <code dir=\"auto\">silent-failure</code> <code dir=\"auto\">false-negative</code> <code dir=\"auto\">absence-is-not-evidence</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-08-03</td><td>A single-port probe cannot distinguish ‘this process is wedged’ from ‘this process is healthy and listening somewhere else’ — and the two look identical in ps: 0% CPU, STAT Ss, flat RSS. A packaged <code dir=\"auto\">local</code> env operator served HTTP 200 on :3071 for 26 minutes and was filed as a 26-minute hang because every probe asked :3055. Includes the falsifier (lsof by PID, not by port), why <code dir=\"auto\">sample</code> settles wedged-vs-idle in one call, and the ambient-PORT leak that aimed it at the wrong port in the first place.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/model-unavailable-after-tier-menu-fix-check-pot-steering\">”model unavailable” after a tier-menu fix? Check POT steering, not the launcher</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">runbook</code> <code dir=\"auto\">steering</code> <code dir=\"auto\">model-tiers</code> <code dir=\"auto\">misdiagnosis</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-07-15</td><td>When cup/kettle spawns keep dying on “selected model unavailable” AFTER a global tier-menu fix (config:tiers-set), the cause is almost never a launcher/orchestrator reload lag — it is a per-pot modelTiers/modelOverrides steering override that still pins the OLD spec and wins over the fixed workspace default.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/no-builtin-blueprint-stale-dist-host-bundle\">”no built-in blueprint” almost always means a stale dist-host bundle</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">blueprints</code> <code dir=\"auto\">routines</code> <code dir=\"auto\">build</code> <code dir=\"auto\">dist-host</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-07-08</td><td>A routine/loader throwing <code dir=\"auto\">no built-in blueprint \"&#x3C;id>\" at .../dist-host/blueprints/&#x3C;id>/blueprint.yaml</code> is a stale-bundle drift, not a missing blueprint — and the loader now falls back to the source package.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/pgbouncer-breaks-getorgpg-env-routed-integration-tests\">”no such database: org_…” — PgBouncer default-on breaks getOrgPg env-routed integration tests</a></td><td>—</td><td>active</td><td>2026-06-22</td><td>On a server-class host (the dev box), pgbouncerEnabled() is default-on, so getOrgPg reroutes to :6432 and ignores a testcontainer DSN — failing any integration test that env-routes getOrgPg at a throwaway DB. Fix - set PAPERCUSP_PGBOUNCER=0.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/on-desktop-sessions-reaper-exemption\">”On-desktop” sessions — reaper hard-exemption + presence flag</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">idle-session-reaper</code> <code dir=\"auto\">presence</code> <code dir=\"auto\">desktop</code> <code dir=\"auto\">wmctrl</code> <code dir=\"auto\">adv_sessions</code> <code dir=\"auto\">on-desktop</code> <code dir=\"auto\">reaper-exemption</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-06-29</td><td>A session whose OS window is currently open on the user’s screen (derived live via wmctrl + adv_sessions.window_id) is “on the desktop”. Such sessions are HARD-EXEMPT from every idle-session-reaper slice (the user kept losing windows they were looking at to the live-idle terminate), and coord:presence + /adv/sessions now expose an <code dir=\"auto\">onDesktop</code> flag so you can “assign these to the agent on the desktop”.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/setup-wizard-submodule-url-mismatch\">”Setup failed” on a fresh clone — a renamed <code dir=\"auto\">.gitmodules</code> URL pointed at a non-existent repo</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">setup-wizard</code> <code dir=\"auto\">dogfood-bootstrap</code> <code dir=\"auto\">submodule</code> <code dir=\"auto\">gitmodules</code> <code dir=\"auto\">git-clone</code> <code dir=\"auto\">papercup-rename</code> <code dir=\"auto\">macos</code> <code dir=\"auto\">release</code> <code dir=\"auto\">root-cause</code> <code dir=\"auto\">gotcha</code> <code dir=\"auto\">EI-3548</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-06-25</td><td>THE root cause of the owner’s recurring ‘Setting up Papercusp workspace failed’: the papercup→papercusp identity rename overreached into .gitmodules and rewrote two submodule URLs (libs/papercusp-db, libs/papercusp-shared) to Papercusp/papercusp-db.git / papercusp-shared.git — repos that were NEVER renamed on GitHub (404). Every FRESH dogfood clone then failed submodule init; the dev box was immune (its .git/config kept the correct papercup-* URLs). Fix: restore the URLs to papercup-db.git/papercup-shared.git + a gitmodules-invariants test that fails CI if a submodule URL goes stale again.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/pg-connection-exhaustion-too-many-clients\">”sorry, too many clients already” — PG connection exhaustion under agent load</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">postgres</code> <code dir=\"auto\">connections</code> <code dir=\"auto\">pool</code> <code dir=\"auto\">performance</code> <code dir=\"auto\">scalability</code> <code dir=\"auto\">resource-profile</code> <code dir=\"auto\">diagnostics</code> <code dir=\"auto\">outage</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-06-17</td><td>When psu / dev:pg_* / the whole MCP surface fail with “sorry, too many clients already”, PostgreSQL has hit max_connections. On a big box the cause is stock max_connections=100 + adaptive pool sizing (pgPoolMax up to ~52 PER org pool, ×2 pools, ×N operator processes). Fix is the host autodetector (resource-profile deriveDatabaseTuning), not a concurrency cap. Diagnose at the OS level because the DB tools are themselves locked out.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/spilled-is-not-omitted-recoverability-in-result-envelopes\">”Spilled” is not “omitted”: read recoverability, not just truncation, off a result envelope</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">result-door</code> <code dir=\"auto\">truncation</code> <code dir=\"auto\">output-envelope</code> <code dir=\"auto\">failure-mode</code> <code dir=\"auto\">reading-results</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-08-31</td><td>A bounded result tells you TWO different things — that it is not the whole answer, and whether the missing bytes still exist. Conflating them is a measured, repeat defect: four independent reports across three tools read <code dir=\"auto\">omittedItems</code> on a result-door spill as data loss when the full content was sitting recoverable in the spill file, and one of them reported a field as unavailable on that basis. How to tell the two apart as a reader, and the rule for producers.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/unresolved-escalation-phantom-orphaned-slug\">”Unresolved escalation in harness X” phantoms: a stale/orphaned harness_escalations row, not a live problem</a></td><td>—</td><td>active</td><td>2026-07-07</td><td>The recurring auto-implement EI ‘Unresolved escalation in harness X’ is almost always a PHANTOM — a harness_shared.harness_escalations row whose escalation is set + supervisor_notes empty, while the underlying condition is long since resolved. The green-checkpoint-{stall,watchdog} variants self-clear via trackGateStall / green-stall-watchdog only when the row’s harness_slug equals the LIVE install-slug; a row keyed under a DEAD/renamed slug (e.g. legacy ‘papercup’ after the papercup→papercusp rename, which has no live green-checkpoint routine) can never be matched by the clear. As of the EI-8396 fix, collectEscalationSignals now SUPPRESSES exactly those two green-checkpoint phases when the row’s install-slug has no live green-checkpoint routine, so a dead-install orphan of those phases no longer loops forever. A stale row under any OTHER phase (or a same-slug row that just never got cleared) still re-fires the watchdog every tick. The drill: confirm the real condition is resolved via routines.gate_health, then clear the stale row (escalation=NULL + supervisor_notes) — do NOT try to ‘fix’ a green gate.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/rate-limit-is-usually-account-routing-not-capacity\">”We hit the rate limit” is usually account-routing, not real capacity</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">llm</code> <code dir=\"auto\">rate-limit</code> <code dir=\"auto\">429</code> <code dir=\"auto\">multi-account</code> <code dir=\"auto\">inference-gateway</code> <code dir=\"auto\">account-routing</code> <code dir=\"auto\">spawn</code> <code dir=\"auto\">governor</code> <code dir=\"auto\">capacity</code> <code dir=\"auto\">debugging</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-06-17</td><td>Papercusp runs LLM inference over a POOL of many Anthropic accounts behind an inference gateway with a per-account rate governor, so a true usage/quota wall is rare. Agents keep mis-reading a routing/config fault as exhaustion (‘we hit the account limit’, ‘session limit’, ‘exceeded max wait’, a 429) and give up. Several faults masquerade as a limit: (1) the account-aware routing is gated behind INFERENCE_GATEWAY + INFERENCE_GATEWAY_MULTI_ACCOUNT flags — OFF → spawned cups get no PAPERCUSP_ACCOUNT_ID → the governor keys the account-BLIND global anthropic:opus bucket → one account’s 429 pauses it fleet-wide even with 6 idle accounts (‘rate-limit pause exceeded max wait’, exit 1, ~30ms, $0); (2) the gateway pools only some accounts — selectSpawnAccount pins a cup to a healthy account via x-papercusp-account, but if that account isn’t in the gateway’s pool the header is ignored and it falls back to its exhausted active() account, so the cup HANGS at $0. Verify with dev:rate_governor_status / accounts:status / the cup’s /proc env / the gateway /healthz before concluding a limit.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/attributing-claude-token-spend\">”What is using my Claude usage?” — query the PG ledger, not processes or transcripts</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">tokens</code> <code dir=\"auto\">cost</code> <code dir=\"auto\">usage</code> <code dir=\"auto\">rate-limit</code> <code dir=\"auto\">accounts</code> <code dir=\"auto\">cron</code> <code dir=\"auto\">routines</code> <code dir=\"auto\">ephemeral-agents</code> <code dir=\"auto\">debugging</code> <code dir=\"auto\">false-negative</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-07-25</td><td>harness_shared.agent_usage_samples is the only authoritative spend ledger. Three independent surfaces return convincing FALSE NEGATIVES: the agents-running roster reads empty because cron routines spawn ephemeral agents that exit between fires; a transcript scan of ~/.claude/projects finds nothing because those roles log usage to PG only; and gateway:owner_report showing 0 successful calls covers only gateway-routed traffic. Conversely, dozens of live claude processes at ~1% CPU can be burning exactly zero. Cost of getting this wrong: two confidently-wrong root causes handed to the owner before the ledger was ever queried.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/pgss-dollar-n-is-normalization-not-a-bind-parameter\">$n in pg_stat_statements is normalization, not a bind parameter — never diagnose sargability from pgss text</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">postgres</code> <code dir=\"auto\">performance</code> <code dir=\"auto\">pg_stat_statements</code> <code dir=\"auto\">false-positive</code> <code dir=\"auto\">measurement</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-09-01</td><td>A run of bare AND $6 AND $7 in a pg_stat_statements entry looks like opaque boolean binds the planner cannot use. It is usually literal TRUE, which Postgres constant-folds — so the obvious dynamic-WHERE fix is pure churn.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/disallowed-tools-cannot-withhold-an-mcp-tool\">—disallowedTools cannot withhold an MCP tool, and a deny looks exactly like never-seeded</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">tools</code> <code dir=\"auto\">confinement</code> <code dir=\"auto\">mcp</code> <code dir=\"auto\">deny-list</code> <code dir=\"auto\">measurement</code> <code dir=\"auto\">psu</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-08-30</td><td>Two traps for anyone trying to confine an MCP surface with —disallowedTools: (a) it is a client-side DISCOVERY control, not a capability boundary — tools:invoke re-reaches a denied papercusp verb in one call, by design; and (b) the observable signature of a deny is byte-identical to a tool that was never seeded, so any deny probe without a same-server control can record a false confirmation.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/tmp-shares-device-with-mnt-data-enospc-false-reds\">/tmp is a bind mount sharing the same device as /mnt/data — ENOSPC there masquerades as N false gate reds</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">runbook</code> <code dir=\"auto\">infra</code> <code dir=\"auto\">green-checkpoint</code> <code dir=\"auto\">release-gate</code> <code dir=\"auto\">testing</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-08-21</td><td>On the dev box, /tmp is a bind mount of a subdir of the SAME XFS filesystem mounted at /mnt/data (a 2TB swapfile + mongodb data + backups live there too). When that device gets tight, vitest workers hit ENOSPC mkdir’ing scratch dirs and every affected suite fails at COLLECTION — indistinguishable at a glance from N real regressions. The gate now runs a preflight (checkDiskHeadroom in green-checkpoint.ts) that refuses with reason=disk-headroom before any suite work when critical write headroom is breached, instead of letting ENOSPC misattribute to the candidate.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/zero-tripwires-means-unarmed-not-broken\">0 autonomy tripwires is the UNARMED dark-ship state, NOT a broken backstop</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">autonomy</code> <code dir=\"auto\">mug</code> <code dir=\"auto\">tripwire</code> <code dir=\"auto\">auto-revert</code> <code dir=\"auto\">decider</code> <code dir=\"auto\">flags</code> <code dir=\"auto\">dark-ship</code> <code dir=\"auto\">verify-first</code> <code dir=\"auto\">decision-ledger</code> <code dir=\"auto\">misdiagnosis</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-06-18</td><td>autonomy_tripwire_list returning 0 does not mean the auto-revert safety net is broken. Tripwires arm ONLY when the autonomy policy is armed (papercusp-mug-autonomy-armed) or papercusp-mug-full-autonomy is ON — both default OFF. Unarmed → the decider returns gated for every action → planReversibleArm returns null → nothing arms, BY DESIGN (D-007). And don’t be fooled by “N auto-actions in the decision ledger”: the action-layer logs every governed call with posture=auto; that is not the same as an autonomy-gated reversible Mug auto-take, and most of the volume is unrelated (in papercusp-workspace ~1000 were the palette command-palette runaway, EI-597). The arm seam is wired only to work_items:set_state + set_priority.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/staging-3170-flaps-every-5min-via-auto-sync-timer\">:3170 connection refusals during staging sync — diagnose the coordinated restart path</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">staging</code> <code dir=\"auto\">3170</code> <code dir=\"auto\">availability</code> <code dir=\"auto\">systemd</code> <code dir=\"auto\">flap</code> <code dir=\"auto\">connection-refused</code> <code dir=\"auto\">restart</code> <code dir=\"auto\">EI-13221</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-07-19</td><td>The staging sync timer can trigger a coordinated :3170 restart when server code changes; SPA-only advances skip it and active clients can defer the sync. The current script uses dev:restart with its drain/coalesce path and verifies the exact served staging SHA.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/pg-connection-exhaustion-fleet-wedge\">\\“too many clients already\\” is a connection storm or pool overhang — diagnose it at the OS level, don’t assume a DB outage</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">postgres</code> <code dir=\"auto\">pg</code> <code dir=\"auto\">max-connections</code> <code dir=\"auto\">connection-storm</code> <code dir=\"auto\">fleet-wedge</code> <code dir=\"auto\">too-many-clients</code> <code dir=\"auto\">hono-host</code> <code dir=\"auto\">staging-api</code> <code dir=\"auto\">debugging</code> <code dir=\"auto\">infra</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-06-17</td><td>Papercusp’s PG is the native cluster /var/lib/postgresql/18/main on :5432 with max_connections=100 (db harness_admin; users papercusp + papercusp_su). You can diagnose + fix entirely at the OS level WITHOUT a SQL connection: count the postmaster’s backends, map each :5432 socket to its owning PID with ss, find the one PID holding hundreds, and kill that subtree (or restart the offending service). Diagnosis + manual-recovery chain inside.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/structured-content-opt-in-ignored-when-format-is-json\">_meta.structured opt-in silently dropped when the chosen format is already JSON</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">mcp</code> <code dir=\"auto\">tooldef</code> <code dir=\"auto\">outputSchema</code> <code dir=\"auto\">structuredContent</code> <code dir=\"auto\">serialize-result</code> <code dir=\"auto\">ptool</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-07-19</td><td>Why an MCP tool with an object-rooted result schema could throw “has an output schema but did not return structured content” even after the caller explicitly opted in via <code dir=\"auto\">_meta.structured</code> — the opt-in was gated on the wrong condition in the one shared serializer.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/await-is-not-a-yield-an-operation-that-starves-its-own-host\"><code dir=\"auto\">await</code> is not a yield — an operation that starves the event loop gets its own host restarted, and reads as merely slow</a></td><td>—</td><td>—</td><td>—</td><td>A loop awaiting promises that resolve in the current tick never reaches the event loop’s timer phase, so every setInterval in the process stops. Don’t read it as “not a regression”; check the warning, or round-trip the store.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/bash-pipefail-grep-q-sigpipe-false-negative\"><code dir=\"auto\">set -o pipefail</code> + <code dir=\"auto\">grep -q</code> short-circuit silently inverts <code dir=\"auto\">{ … } | grep -q &#x26;&#x26; …</code></a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">bash</code> <code dir=\"auto\">shell</code> <code dir=\"auto\">pipefail</code> <code dir=\"auto\">footgun</code> <code dir=\"auto\">gotcha</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-07-19</td><td>Under <code dir=\"auto\">set -o pipefail</code>, a <code dir=\"auto\">{ producer; } | grep -q PATTERN &#x26;&#x26; action</code> pipeline returns NON-ZERO on a match when grep -q short-circuits and the upstream producer takes SIGPIPE — so the <code dir=\"auto\">&#x26;&#x26;</code> action misfires and a real match reads as “no match”. Use capture-then-here-string instead.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/connection-closed-6432-is-an-idle-tx-kill-not-pgbouncer\"><code dir=\"auto\">write CONNECTION_CLOSED 127.0.0.1:6432</code> is an idle-tx kill, not a PgBouncer bug — and how to prove a fix with a :3170-vs-:3070 A/B</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">mcp</code> <code dir=\"auto\">postgres</code> <code dir=\"auto\">pgbouncer</code> <code dir=\"auto\">idle-in-transaction</code> <code dir=\"auto\">tools-invoke</code> <code dir=\"auto\">two-port</code> <code dir=\"auto\">verification</code> <code dir=\"auto\">runbook</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-07-27</td><td>The :6432 in the error names the pooler, so this signature has been mis-filed as a PgBouncer problem at least three times. It is Postgres killing a backend at idle_in_transaction_session_timeout (60s) because the MCP dispatcher held a workspace tx open across slow NON-DB work. The tell is a duration of almost exactly 60000ms. Fixing the inner tool is a no-op while a DELEGATOR (tools:invoke) wraps it in its own tx. Also documents the general technique: use :3170 (your edit) vs :3070 (green release) as a controlled A/B to prove a server-side fix before it deploys.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/coord-log-furnace-ei-is-usually-stale-pgss-debris\">A “coord_event_log furnace” EI is usually stale pg_stat_statements debris, not a live bug</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">coordination</code> <code dir=\"auto\">furnace</code> <code dir=\"auto\">pg_stat_statements</code> <code dir=\"auto\">triage</code> <code dir=\"auto\">auto-implement</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-07-11</td><td>Triage recipe for the recurring “coord invariant: unbounded coord_event_log read pattern (furnace class)” EI — verify against live pg_stat_statements min_exec_time before assuming a live unbounded scan.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/verifying-prod-from-the-dev-box-resolves-to-localhost\">A “prod” check from the dev box can silently verify localhost</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">verification</code> <code dir=\"auto\">dns</code> <code dir=\"auto\">false-green</code> <code dir=\"auto\">hooks</code> <code dir=\"auto\">browser-checks</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-08-17</td><td>/etc/hosts pins some *.papercusp.com names to 127.0.0.1, so a prod curl/verdict check returns a clean 200 from the local server with no tell in the response — and the —resolve workaround times out because the LAN also drops *.papercusp.com TLS. the <code dir=\"auto\">workspace.workScope</code> state cell and the /admin/work-scope door (WI-2145092); how to reach the tool before :3070 carries the code; the boot-prime and hive-guard caveats.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/cross-workspace-tools-and-workspace-required\">Workspace-agnostic tools need <code dir=\"auto\">crossWorkspace: true</code> (or they fail on fleet sessions)</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">agent-tools</code> <code dir=\"auto\">defineTool</code> <code dir=\"auto\">workspace</code> <code dir=\"auto\">memory</code> <code dir=\"auto\">fleet</code> <code dir=\"auto\">gotcha</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-06-14</td><td>A tool whose data isn’t scoped by a workspace transaction (memory:<em>, list_workspaces, audit:</em>) must declare crossWorkspace:true, or the projected gate throws workspace_required on any UNSCOPED psu/fleet session — even though the call is perfectly valid.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/workspace-scoped-memory-recall\">Workspace-scoped memory recall (the per-owner user-pool bleed fix)</a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">memory</code> <code dir=\"auto\">recall</code> <code dir=\"auto\">workspace-isolation</code> <code dir=\"auto\">mem0</code> <code dir=\"auto\">scope-keys</code> <code dir=\"auto\">flags</code> <code dir=\"auto\">data-scoping</code></td><td>active</td><td>2026-06-24</td><td>Memory recall fans out over opaque SCOPE KEYS (user.id | harness:<slug> | pot:<slug>), not a workspace column — so the per-owner user pool is recalled in every workspace and a pot’s <code dir=\"auto\">project</code> learnings bleed across all the owner’s work. Start Xvfb with -noreset and verify the root property separately.</td></tr><tr><td><a href=\"/internal/docs/agent-insights/claude-oauth-authorize-url\">You CANNOT hand-build a Claude Max OAuth link — claude.ai needs claude-code’s own handshake; use <code dir=\"auto\">claude setup-token</code></a></td><td><code dir=\"auto\">oauth</code> <code dir=\"auto\">claude</code> <code dir=\"auto\">max-account</code> <code dir=\"auto\">accounts-pool</code> <code dir=\"auto\">deploy-accounts</code> <code dir=\"auto\">external-api</code> <code dir=\"auto\">dead-end</code></td><td>superseded</td><td>2026-06-16</td><td>Linking a Claude Max account by having the owner click a hand-built claude.ai authorize URL does NOT work — claude.ai returns “Authorization failed Invalid request format” even for a URL byte-for-byte identical to what <code dir=\"auto\">claude setup-token</code> generates. claude.ai requires the claude-code client’s own handshake, which a plain browser click can’t reproduce. Wiping the AppDir does NOT fix it (tauri just refills the AppDir from the stale staging dir). The deb is immune because dpkg archives fresh from the source. Fix: rm -rf target/release/{sidecar,seed,resources} before the tauri appimage build; a fail-closed --scan-dir gate on the assembled AppDir is the backstop. |\napps/operator/public/internal/docs/agent-insights/mcp-cli-retained-owner-native-incarnation.html:74:<p>During the October3 non-P2P fleet restoration, the same owner had multiple Codex incarnations. Holding owner, endpoint and payload constant and forwarding the actual CODEX_SESSION_ID as native_session made the request succeed. This was a transport identity defect, not evidence that the current leader lacked authority. {"timestamp":"2026-10-10T00:57:08.786Z","ordinal":134,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a1234b-2ad5-7db0-86b8-4dcb0f9aa366","turn_id":"01a1234b-920f-7162-ae53-44f9a71eca46","item":{"type":"CommandExecution","id":"exec-a3685b7a-8dcc-4fa5-b8f6-290ce12c579f","process_id":"56285","command":["/bin/bash","-lc","sed -n '600,690p' packages/operator-core/lib/capability-envelope/identity-grants-port.test.ts"],"cwd":"file:///home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp","parsed_cmd":[{"type":"read","cmd":"sed -n '600,690p' packages/operator-core/lib/capability-envelope/identity-grants-port.test.ts","name":"identity-grants-port.test.ts","path":"packages/operator-core/lib/capability-envelope/identity-grants-port.test.ts"}],"source":"unified_exec_startup","status":"completed","aggregated_output":"    expect(await checkIdentityGrantKernel({ ...f.request, toolName: 'coord:orient' }, unacknowledged, null, read))\n      .toBeNull();\n    expect(read).not.toHaveBeenCalled();\n\n    // Control: the SAME missing row with an acknowledged receipt is still the fault.\n    expect(await checkIdentityGrantKernel(f.request, { ...f.state, identityLaunchRecordMissing: true }, null, read))\n      .toMatchObject({ decision: 'deny', obligations: { capabilityUnsatisfied: { cause: 'no-launch-record' } } });\n  });\n\n  // WI-10002028: the recovery door must not ride the failure domain it recovers.\n  // `stale-artifact` does not say \"this session lacks authority for coord:orient\";\n  // it says \"we cannot establish WHICH specification is in force\". Denying the\n  // resync verb on that basis is self-sealing: coord:orient({afterCompaction:true})\n  // is the only caller of acknowledgeControlTransition (orient.ts), so it is the\n  // one verb that can converge the activation — and the preflight was holding it\n  // shut. The live consequence was a session bricked for its entire life, with\n  // BOTH documented toolless fallbacks denied (scripts/mcp-call.mjs reaches the\n  // same server-side preflight, so changing client/port/transport cannot help),\n  // recoverable only by an undocumented sudo psql UPDATE.\n  //\n  // Opening it is not a widening: the door already opens with NO launch record at\n  // all (the test above), which is strictly LESS identity evidence than a record\n  // that replays but whose `applied` pointer is unresolved. Anyone able to tamper\n  // a record into this state could equally delete it and take the weaker door, so\n  // gating on artifact integrity protected nothing and bricked honest sessions.\n  // Authority is unchanged either way: `applied:false` confers no grants.\n  it('keeps the coord:orient recovery door open for every stale-artifact shape', async () => {\n    const f = fixture();\n    const stranded = fixture({ requires: [] });\n    // Each entry is a distinct shape that reaches a `stale-artifact` denial.\n    const shapes: Array<[string, unknown, unknown]> = [\n      // `applied` names a specification no receipt in the record can produce —\n      // the exact residue of a relaunch-with-carry (applied stuck on the PREVIOUS\n      // session's revision while the successor runs a new one).\n      ['unresolvable applied receipt', { activation: { applied: stranded.applied } }, f.record],\n      // Artifact tampering: the replayed specification disagrees with the record.\n      ['tampered artifact', f.state, { ...f.record, specificationArtifact: { ...f.artifact, configuration: {} } }],\n      // A record that is absent without being flagged as explicitly missing.\n      ['absent record', f.state, null],\n    ];\n\n    for (const [label, state, record] of shapes) {\n      const read = vi.fn(async () => f.policy);\n      expect(await checkIdentityGrantKernel(\n        { ...f.request, toolName: 'coord:orient' }, state as never, record, read,\n      ), label).toMatchObject({ decision: 'allow', code: 'identity-recovery', applied: false });\n\n      // Calibration: the SAME shape must still fail closed for an ordinary tool.\n      // Without this, a blanket allow would pass the assertion above.\n      expect(await checkIdentityGrantKernel(f.request, state as never, record, read), label)\n        .toMatchObject({ decision: 'deny', obligations: { capabilityUnsatisfied: { cause: 'stale-artifact' } } });\n    }\n  });\n\n  // The door above is keyed on the tool NAME, and on the path that actually\n  // bricks sessions the name never matches. A TRIMMED su surface does not carry\n  // coord:orient in its seed, so the only route to the door is\n  // `tools:invoke { name: 'coord:orient' }` — the gate saw `tools:invoke`, the\n  // comparison failed, and the door stayed shut. Measured live 2026-09-20T10:43Z\n  // by su-56d0a9bd, who had shipped the previous fix and was still bricked by\n  // this on the first call of their next life (\"that fix could not have saved me\").\n  it('opens the recovery door for the dispatch wrapper carrying coord:orient', async () => {\n    const f = fixture();\n    const stranded = fixture({ requires: [] });\n    const shapes: Array<[string, unknown, unknown]> = [\n      ['unresolvable applied receipt', { activation: { applied: stranded.applied } }, f.record],\n      ['tampered artifact', f.state, { ...f.record, specificationArtifact: { ...f.artifact, configuration: {} } }],\n      ['absent record', f.state, null],\n    ];\n\n    for (const [label, state, record] of shapes) {\n      const read = vi.fn(async () => f.policy);\n      const wrapped = {\n        ...f.request,\n        toolName: IDENTITY_BREAK_GLASS.dispatchWrapper,\n        args: { name: 'coord:orient', args: {} },\n      };\n      expect(await checkIdentityGrantKernel(wrapped, state as never, record, read), label)\n        .toMatchObject({ decision: 'allow', code: 'identity-recovery', applied: false });\n\n      // Calibration, and the control that keeps this a DOOR rather than a hole:\n      // admitting the WRAPPER itself would make the entire catalogue reachable\n      // through it. The declared target must decide, not the wrapper's presence.\n      const ordinary = {\n        ...f.request,\n        toolName: IDENTITY_BREAK_GLASS.dispatchWrapper,\n        args: { name: 'work_items:complete', args: {} },\n      };\n      expect(await checkIdentityGrantKernel(ordinary, state as never, record, read), label)\n        .toMatchObject({ decision: 'deny' });\n    }\n","exit_code":0,"duration":{"secs":0,"nanos":31641}},"started_at_ms":1791593828786,"completed_at_ms":1791593828786}}
{"timestamp":"2026-10-10T00:57:08.799Z","ordinal":135,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a1234b-2ad5-7db0-86b8-4dcb0f9aa366","turn_id":"01a1234b-920f-7162-ae53-44f9a71eca46","item":{"type":"CommandExecution","id":"exec-132db01a-c951-4edc-b479-8372867121d6","process_id":"52110","command":["/bin/bash","-lc","sed -n '560,640p' packages/operator-core/lib/capability-envelope/identity-grants-port.ts"],"cwd":"file:///home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp","parsed_cmd":[{"type":"read","cmd":"sed -n '560,640p' packages/operator-core/lib/capability-envelope/identity-grants-port.ts","name":"identity-grants-port.ts","path":"packages/operator-core/lib/capability-envelope/identity-grants-port.ts"}],"source":"unified_exec_startup","status":"completed","aggregated_output":" * cause here protects EVERY denial site at once; the companion test asserts the\n * implication across all of them rather than a hand-listed few.\n */\nexport const IDENTITY_BREAK_GLASS: {\n  readonly tool: string;\n  readonly causes: readonly IdentityGrantFailure['cause'][];\n  /**\n   * The single-target dispatch wrapper that forwards ONE named tool server-side.\n   *\n   * WI-10002028 shipped the door keyed on the tool name alone, and it could not\n   * open on the path that actually bricks sessions: a TRIMMED su surface does not\n   * carry {@link IDENTITY_RECOVERY_TOOL} in its seed, so the only way to reach the\n   * recovery door is `tools:invoke { name: 'coord:orient' }`. The gate then sees\n   * `tools:invoke`, the name comparison fails, and the door stays shut — measured\n   * live 2026-09-20T10:43Z by su-56d0a9bd, whose own fix could not save them.\n   *\n   * Admitting the wrapper confers NOTHING on its own: `tools:invoke` forwards\n   * through `ctx.dispatchTool`, so the inner tool runs its own full kernel\n   * preflight and is gated exactly as a direct call. The outer denial therefore\n   * protected nothing while making the brick permanent.\n   */\n  readonly dispatchWrapper: string;\n} = {\n  tool: IDENTITY_RECOVERY_TOOL,\n  causes: ['stale-artifact', 'no-launch-record'],\n  dispatchWrapper: RECOVERY_DOOR_DISPATCH_WRAPPER,\n};\n\n/**\n * WI-10002028: of every cause this port can raise, `stale-artifact` is the one\n * that is NOT a statement about the session's authority — it says the identity\n * plane cannot establish WHICH specification is in force. Refusing\n * {@link IDENTITY_RECOVERY_TOOL} on that basis makes the failure self-sealing:\n * every tool is denied, including the door the CTRL block's own `resync`\n * contract names, and BOTH documented toolless fallbacks reach this same\n * server-side preflight (scripts/mcp-call.mjs is a different transport, not a\n * different gate), so changing client, port or transport cannot open it.\n * Recovery then required an out-of-band sudo psql write.\n *\n * A recovery door must not ride the failure domain it recovers. Pure and exported so\n * the direct-vs-proxy distinction cannot silently collapse back to one number.\n */\nexport function ptoolConnectAttemptTimeoutMs(operatorUrl, env = process.env) {\n  try {\n    const url = new URL(operatorUrl);\n    const local = url.hostname === '127.0.0.1' || url.hostname === 'localhost' || url.hostname === '::1';\n    if (!local) return PTOOL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS;\n\n    const configuredProxyBase = typeof env.PAPERCUSP_MCP_PROXY_BASE === 'string'\n      ? env.PAPERCUSP_MCP_PROXY_BASE.trim()\n      : '';\n    if (configuredProxyBase && new URL(configuredProxyBase).origin === url.origin) {\n      return PTOOL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS;\n    }\n    const configuredProxyPort = Number(env.PAPERCUSP_MCP_PROXY_PORT);\n    const proxyPort = Number.isInteger(configuredProxyPort) && configuredProxyPort > 0\n      ? configuredProxyPort\n      : 9071;\n    if (Number(url.port) === proxyPort) return PTOOL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS;\n  } catch {\n    // connectWithLocalRetry/connect() will surface the malformed URL. Do not\n    // turn input validation into an unrelated timeout-policy error here.\n    return PTOOL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS;\n  }\n  return Math.min(PTOOL_DIRECT_CONNECT_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS, PTOOL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS);\n}\n\n// The proxy's handshake bulkhead returns a retryable HTTP 429 while all\n// handshake slots are occupied. Keep the attempt ceiling aligned with the\n// complete client budget: a fixed 30-attempt ceiling plus a one-second delay\n// silently shortened the 120s recovery window to ~30s, so a busy fleet could\n// exhaust ptool before a slot became available (EI-21395813315545528).\nexport const PTOOL_CONNECT_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 1_000;\nexport const PTOOL_CONNECT_MAX_ATTEMPTS = Math.ceil(\n  PTOOL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS / PTOOL_CONNECT_RETRY_DELAY_MS,\n) + 1;\n\n// Explicit/local direct URLs remain pinned, but a hard operator restart can\n// briefly refuse connections. Give those pins one short recovery window: one\n// direct-handshake timeout plus five paced retry intervals (20s with the\n// current budgets), bounded independently from the managed/proxy 120s window.\n","exit_code":0,"duration":{"secs":0,"nanos":25559}},"started_at_ms":1791593842587,"completed_at_ms":1791593842587}}

Network implementations wrap the same failure\n * in ordinary fetch/socket errors, so keep the code and message checks together\n * rather than treating every rejected tools/call as replayable.\n */\nexport function isTransportFailure(error) {\n  const codes = [error?.code, error?.cause?.code];\n  if (codes.some((code) => code === -32000 || code === -32001)) return true;\n  const detail = errorDetail(error);\n  return /(?:fetch failed|econn(?:reset|refused|aborted)|etimedout|epipe|en[et]unreach|und_err_socket|socket (?:hang up|closed|reset|error)|(?:connection|transport|stream) (?:closed|reset|aborted|failed)|other side closed|network error)/i.test(detail);\n}\n\n/**\n * An HTTP response proves that the local endpoint answered. Retrying it as a\n * connection failure is both wasteful and misleading: in particular, the MCP\n * proxy's 503 is the authoritative, typed result after it has already spent\n * its full restart-absorption window. Walk `cause` because connect() adds\n * operator guidance around the SDK's StreamableHTTPError.\n */\nexport function isExplicitHttpConnectFailure(error) {\n  const seen = new Set();\n  let current = error;\n  while (current && (typeof current === 'object' || typeof current === 'function')) {\n    if (seen.has(current)) break;\n    seen.add(current);\n    const status = Number(current.code);\n    if (Number.isInteger(status) && status >= 400 && status <= 599) return true;\n    current = current.cause;\n  }\n  return false;\n}\n\n/**\n * A reachable staging listener may run an older control-plane build that\n * cannot read this session's authority. Generous so a normally-firing fleet\n * (git-sync alone fires every few minutes) never false-alarms, while a real freeze\n * (tens of minutes) trips it. Isolates \"ticker frozen (ALL routines stop)\" from \"one\n * routine stuck\" — the latter is git-pipeline-stats / the green-stall-watchdog.\n */\nexport const BG_HOST_STALE_MS = 15 * 60_000;\n\n/**\n * The probe names emitted WITHOUT an `EndpointSpec` — the \"portless\" probes.\n * `HEALTH_ENDPOINTS` enumerates every fixed-URL probe, so it is the natural\n * answer to \"is this a real probe target?\"; these names are the rest of that\n * answer, and nothing else enumerated them.\n *\n * LOAD-BEARING, not a doc list: the emitters below name themselves FROM this\n * constant, so it cannot drift from what is actually emitted.
