It is listed because the guard needs\n * the complete set, and is the reason this is a name TABLE rather than a set\n * derived from the emitters themselves.\n */\nexport const PORTLESS_PROBE_NAMES = {\n  /** Emitted by the desktop-shell probe, outside this module. */\n  desktop: 'desktop',\n  bgHostTicker: 'bg-host-ticker',\n  bgHostCode: 'bg-host-code',\n  mcpProxyCode: 'mcp-proxy-code',\n  mcpProxyBgHostCode: 'mcp-proxy-bg-host-code',\n  substrateSidecar: 'substrate-sidecar',\n  embedSidecar: 'embed-sidecar',\n  /** See {@link probeJournalCanary} (EI-15810, EI-2434 follow-up). */\n  journalCanary: 'journal-canary',\n} as const;\n\n/** Flat lookup for \"is this name a portless probe target?\" */\nexport const PORTLESS_PROBE_NAME_SET: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set<string>(\n  Object.values(PORTLESS_PROBE_NAMES),\n);\n\n/**\n * The health probe must fit inside the interactive query-embedding budget.\n * A successful /healthz response only proves that the sidecar's HTTP listener\n * is alive; it does not prove that the model worker can accept an embed. Keep\n * the functional request deliberately tiny and bounded so a saturated worker\n * cannot stall the service-health tick.\n */\nexport const EMBED_SIDECAR_FUNCTIONAL_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 1_200;\nconst EMBED_SIDECAR_FUNCTIONAL_PROBE_TEXT = 'health probe';\n\n/**\n * WI-1647443 — the probe text is a CONSTANT, and the sidecar caches on\n * `${model}:${kind}\\0${text}`. A local fork from the multi-GB bg-host blocks\n * its main thread for time proportional to its RSS; a 30 s profile put probeCodeDrift at 47%\n * of the main thread's spawn self time.\n *\n * The probe is fail-soft (any error ⇒ present:false), so a regression to a raw execFile would\n * not throw — the seam would simply stop being called. This drives the WHOLE probe and asserts\n * that each of its four spawns reached the seam AND that the answer was built from the seam's\n * output (the newest file / identity leg), not from a fail-soft fallback.\n */\nimport { hostname } from 'node:os';\nimport { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';\n\nconst BOOT_MS = 1_790_000_000_000;\nconst LOADED_SHA = 'b'.repeat(40);\nconst HEAD_SHA = 'c'.repeat(40);\n\nconst { execFileViaSidecar, boundedPgReadTxn } = vi.hoisted(() => ({\n  execFileViaSidecar: vi.fn(),\n  boundedPgReadTxn: vi.fn(),\n}));\nvi.mock('./fleet/git-via-sidecar', async (importOriginal) => ({\n  ...(await importOriginal<typeof import('./fleet/git-via-sidecar')>()),\n  execFileViaSidecar,\n}));\nvi.mock('./pg-read-query', async (importOriginal) => ({\n  ...(await importOriginal<typeof import('./pg-read-query')>()),\n  boundedPgReadTxn,\n}));\nvi.mock('./agent-tools/dev/systemd-service-probe', async (importOriginal) => ({\n  ...(await importOriginal<typeof import('./agent-tools/dev/systemd-service-probe')>()),\n  probeServiceStart: vi.fn(async () => ({ ok: true, mainPid: 4242, startedAtMs: 1_790_000_000_000 })),\n}));\n\nfunction seamResponse(cmd: string, args: string[]): { stdout: string; stderr: string } {\n  if (cmd === 'git' && args.join(' ') === 'rev-parse --show-toplevel') return { stdout: '/repo\\n', stderr: '' };\n  if (cmd === 'git' && args.join(' ') === 'rev-parse HEAD') return { stdout: `${HEAD_SHA}\\n`, stderr: '' };\n  if (cmd === 'git' && args[0] === 'diff') return { stdout: 'packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/x.ts\\n', stderr: '' };\n  if (cmd === 'find') return { stdout: `${(BOOT_MS + 120_000) / 1000} packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/x.ts\\n`, stderr: '' };\n  throw new Error(`unexpected spawn: ${cmd} ${args.join(' ')}`);\n}\n\nconst prevRoot = process.env.PAPERCUSP_INTEGRATION_ROOT;\n\nbeforeEach(() => {\n  delete process.env.PAPERCUSP_INTEGRATION_ROOT;\n  execFileViaSidecar.mockReset();\n  execFileViaSidecar.mockImplementation(async (cmd: string, args: string[]) => seamResponse(cmd, args));\n  boundedPgReadTxn.mockReset();\n  boundedPgReadTxn.mockResolvedValue([\n    {\n      host: hostname(),\n      pid: 4242,\n      reportedAt: new {"timestamp":"2026-10-10T01:06:52.124Z","ordinal":414,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a1234b-2ad5-7db0-86b8-4dcb0f9aa366","turn_id":"01a1234b-920f-7162-ae53-44f9a71eca46","item":{"type":"CommandExecution","id":"exec-722ef524-55a5-40e7-91e0-dfc08751a272","process_id":"14672","command":["/bin/bash","-lc","sed -n '1160,1270p' packages/operator-core/lib/service-health.ts"],"cwd":"file:///home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp","parsed_cmd":[{"type":"read","cmd":"sed -n '1160,1270p' packages/operator-core/lib/service-health.ts","name":"service-health.ts","path":"packages/operator-core/lib/service-health.ts"}],"source":"unified_exec_startup","status":"completed","aggregated_output":"\nfunction isGitSha(value: string): boolean {\n  return /^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/i.test(value.trim());\n}\n\nconst CODE_DRIFT_TEST_EXCLUDE_PATHSPEC = ':(exclude)**/*.test.ts';\n\n/**\n * Compare two committed identities only in the files a service actually loads.\n *\n * A runtime-vintage `treeSha` is a whole-repository commit identity. Comparing it\n * directly with the current whole-repository HEAD makes every unrelated commit\n * look like service code drift. `git diff --name-only ... -- <hot paths>` keeps\n * the committed leg in the same scope as the mtime leg. `null` is deliberate:\n * an unavailable/unknown Git ref must not be interpreted as \"no drift\".\n */\nexport async function compareCommittedHotPaths(\n  run: CodeDriftExecFile,\n  integrationRoot: string,\n  loadedSha: string,\n  currentSha: string,\n  hotPaths: readonly string[],\n): Promise<boolean | null> {\n  const loaded = loadedSha.trim();\n  const current = currentSha.trim();\n  if (!isGitSha(loaded) || !isGitSha(current) || hotPaths.length === 0) return null;\n  if (sameSourceSha(loaded, current)) return false;\n  try {\n    const { stdout } = await run(\n      'git',\n      ['diff', '--name-only', loaded, current, '--', ...hotPaths, CODE_DRIFT_TEST_EXCLUDE_PATHSPEC],\n      { cwd: integrationRoot, timeout: 3000, maxBuffer: 4 * 1024 * 1024 },\n    );\n    return stdout.trim().length > 0;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction identityLabel(identity: LoadedCodeIdentity): string {\n  const pid = identity.pid == null ? '' : ` pid ${identity.pid}`;\n  const host = identity.host ? ` on ${identity.host}` : '';\n  const reported = identity.reportedAt ? ` reported ${identity.reportedAt}` : '';\n  return `runtime-vintage${pid}${host}${reported}`;\n}\n\n/** Probe bg-host code drift (WI-1867): unit MainPID elapsed-seconds vs the newest\n *  *.ts mtime under BG_HOST_HOT_PATHS in the integration tree (the working tree the\n *  bg-host tsx-loads from — mtime, not commit time, is what a restart would pick up).\n *  Fail-soft at every step (no systemd / no unit / no tree ⇒ present:false, never a\n *  phantom drift). */\nexport async function probeBgHostCodeDrift(now: number = Date.now()): Promise<ProbeResult> {\n  return probeCodeDrift(\n    {\n      name: PORTLESS_PROBE_NAMES.bgHostCode,\n      unit: process.env.PAPERCUSP_BGHOST_WATCHDOG_UNIT || 'papercusp-bg-host',\n      hotPaths: BG_HOST_HOT_PATHS,\n      artifactPaths: BG_HOST_ARTIFACT_PATHS,\n      evaluate: evaluateBgHostCodeDrift,\n      platformNote: 'bg-host code-drift probe is Linux/systemd-only — not applicable on this platform',\n      failedNote: 'bg-host code-drift unknown (probe failed)',\n    },\n    now,\n  );\n}\n\n/** Probe :9071 MCP-proxy code drift (EI-21390665295968159): the `papercup-mcp-proxy` unit's\n *  start time vs the newest *.ts mtime under {@link MCP_PROXY_HOT_PATHS} in the tree it\n *  tsx-loads from. Same fail-soft contract as the bg-host probe — no systemd / no unit /\n *  no tree ⇒ present:false, never a phantom drift. */\nexport async function probeMcpProxyCodeDrift(now: number = Date.now()): Promise<ProbeResult> {\n  return probeCodeDrift(\n    {\n      name: PORTLESS_PROBE_NAMES.mcpProxyCode,\n      unit: process.env.PAPERCUSP_MCP_PROXY_UNIT || 'papercup-mcp-proxy',\n      hotPaths: MCP_PROXY_HOT_PATHS,\n      evaluate: evaluateMcpProxyCodeDrift,\n      platformNote: 'mcp-proxy code-drift probe is Linux/systemd-only — not applicable on this platform',\n      failedNote: 'mcp-proxy code-drift unknown (probe failed)',\n    },\n    now,\n  );\n}\n\n/** Probe the separate :9271 BG-host MCP proxy against the same source tree. */\nexport async function probeMcpProxyBgHostCodeDrift(now: number = Date.now()): Promise<ProbeResult> {\n  return probeCodeDrift(\n    {\n      name: PORTLESS_PROBE_NAMES.mcpProxyBgHostCode,\n      unit: 'papercup-mcp-proxy-bg-host',\n      hotPaths: MCP_PROXY_BG_HOST_HOT_PATHS,\n      evaluate: evaluateMcpProxyBgHostCodeDrift,\n      platformNote: 'BG-host mcp-proxy code-drift probe is Linux/systemd-only — not applicable on this platform',\n      failedNote: 'BG-host mcp-proxy code-drift unknown (probe failed)',\n    },\n    now,\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * Keep the runtime-vintage lookup inside the same bounded read-only transaction\n * used by the other operator diagnostics. Comparing it\\n * directly with the current whole-repository HEAD makes every unrelated commit\\n * look like service code drift. `git diff --name-only ... -- <hot paths>` keeps\\n * the committed leg in the same scope as the mtime leg. `null` is deliberate:\\n * an unavailable/unknown Git ref must not be interpreted as \\\"no drift\\\".\\n */\\nexport async function compareCommittedHotPaths(\\n  run: CodeDriftExecFile,\\n  integrationRoot: string,\\n  loadedSha: string,\\n  currentSha: string,\\n  hotPaths: readonly string[],\\n): Promise<boolean | null> {\\n  const loaded = loadedSha.trim();\\n  const current = currentSha.trim();\\n  if (!isGitSha(loaded) || !isGitSha(current) || hotPaths.length === 0) return null;\\n  if (sameSourceSha(loaded, current)) return false;\\n  try {\\n    const { stdout } = await run(\\n      'git',\\n      ['diff', '--name-only', loaded, current, '--', ...hotPaths, CODE_DRIFT_TEST_EXCLUDE_PATHSPEC],\\n      { cwd: integrationRoot, timeout: 3000, maxBuffer: 4 * 1024 * 1024 },\\n    );\\n    return stdout.trim().length > 0;\\n  } catch {\\n    return null;\\n  }\\n}\\n\\nfunction identityLabel(identity: LoadedCodeIdentity): string {\\n  const pid = identity.pid == null ? '' : ` pid ${identity.pid}`;\\n  const host = identity.host ? ` on ${identity.host}` : '';\\n  const reported = identity.reportedAt ? ` reported ${identity.reportedAt}` : '';\\n  return `runtime-vintage${pid}${host}${reported}`;\\n}\\n\\n/** Probe bg-host code drift (WI-1867): unit MainPID elapsed-seconds vs the newest\\n *  *.ts mtime under BG_HOST_HOT_PATHS in the integration tree (the working tree the\\n *  bg-host tsx-loads from — mtime, not commit time, is what a restart would pick up).\\n *  Fail-soft at every step (no systemd / no unit / no tree ⇒ present:false, never a\\n *  phantom drift). */\\nexport async function probeBgHostCodeDrift(now: number = Date.now()): Promise<ProbeResult> {\\n  return probeCodeDrift(\\n    {\\n      name: PORTLESS_PROBE_NAMES.bgHostCode,\\n      unit: process.env.PAPERCUSP_BGHOST_WATCHDOG_UNIT || 'papercusp-bg-host',\\n      hotPaths: BG_HOST_HOT_PATHS,\\n      artifactPaths: BG_HOST_ARTIFACT_PATHS,\\n      evaluate: evaluateBgHostCodeDrift,\\n      platformNote: 'bg-host code-drift probe is Linux/systemd-only — not applicable on this platform',\\n      failedNote: 'bg-host code-drift unknown (probe failed)',\\n    },\\n    now,\\n  );\\n}\\n\\n/** Probe :9071 MCP-proxy code drift (EI-21390665295968159): the `papercup-mcp-proxy` unit's\\n *  start time vs the newest *.ts mtime under {@link MCP_PROXY_HOT_PATHS} in the tree it\\n *  tsx-loads from.
